rules.R01: Every request/result struct starts with struct_size, abi_major=0, abi_minor=1; smaller mandatory prefix or wrong major fails.
rules.R03: input_valid_count is 1..160; below 160 only with AS_FRAME_FINAL_INPUT; zero-length streams go straight to drain.
rules.R04: All valid input samples are finite; no facade clipping is documented.
rules.R05: Final-frame padding beyond input_valid_count is exactly zero.
rules.R06: Output capacity >=160, non-null, naturally aligned and non-overlapping; invalid output never triggers a speculative write.
rules.R07: Only the processing lifecycle accepts process/submit; after FINAL_INPUT or drain begin they are rejected; needs_reset blocks them.
rules.R08: Epoch must match and the next input position must be exact; rejection never advances state or counters.
rules.R09: Inconsistent provider counts/intervals or nonfinite provider output become AS_BACKEND_FAILURE and needs_reset.
rules.R10: On rejection, accepted/submitted counters and next_input are unchanged; a valid output buffer is zeroed only for a frame-side rejection.
rules.R11: On success produced_count=160, valid_count=input_valid_count, source_first_sample=n-D; only the first 160 output samples are written.
rules.R12: Buffered submit/pull use a 3-frame FIFO; empty pull is AS_NOT_READY with zero produced/valid count; full submit is AS_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.
rules.R13: AS_END_OF_STREAM only after a completed drain; repeated drain is EOS with zero counts and never an ordinary success frame.
rules.R14: Reset requires a strictly greater epoch; reset while draining cancels the old accepted intervals before clearing state.
rules.R15: Close nulls the handle and all later calls fail AS_CLOSED; separate sessions are uncoupled.
